en.name: Eucharistic Miracle of Florence
en.summary: Consecrated hosts stolen in a church robbery were reportedly found undamaged and glowing where the thief discarded them, decades before Corpus Christi was instituted.
en.body: According to tradition, in 1230, thieves broke into a church in Florence, Italy, and stole a pyx containing consecrated hosts along with other valuables from the altar, discarding the hosts themselves once the more obviously valuable items had been removed. The discarded hosts were reportedly found some time later in a nearby field or hidden corner, undamaged and said to be surrounded by a visible glow that drew the attention of those who came upon them, leading to their recovery and return to the Church with considerable solemnity. The event, predating the institution of the universal Feast of Corpus Christi by several decades, contributed to the strong tradition of Eucharistic devotion already present in Florence, and the recovered relics were enshrined and venerated by the local community in the years that followed.
